topology_reasoning.material_and_layer: The black connected material is a single layer-(1,0) waveguide network; the white regions are the large loop cavities and four rectangular coupling windows.
observations: The outer boundary is a tall, smoothly rounded racetrack with approximately 0.5 um waveguide width and a narrow vertical waist at the left and right sides.

Two matching inner assemblies sit above and below the centerline. Each assembly has two rectangular windows separated by a short common wall, with straight top and bottom rails and tapered side junctions.
The inner assemblies join the outer racetrack through symmetric diagonal side transitions, producing three large white cavities and four small rectangular windows.
The target is vertically symmetric to raster precision, so the base differential path knob is zero while remaining available for measured retargeting.
The dominant fidelity controls are waveguide width, outer racetrack radius/superellipse power, inner cavity dimensions, window gap, rail length, and side-junction taper length.
topology_reasoning.working_model: A primitive-only union of one rounded outer loop, two paired rectangular inner loops, and four diagonal/tapered junction rails.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitive model: rounded outer loop, two two-window rectangular inner assemblies, and four diagonal junction paths.
Replaced the early-turn rounded rectangle with a superellipse outer loop and narrowed junction paths from 0.40 um to 0.28 um.
Trial with superellipse power 2.5 and waveguide width 0.52 um; rejected because the outer curve and footprint worsened.
Returned to 0.50 um width, shifted the inner assembly laterally with a 0.89 um rail span, and set the outer superellipse power to 3.5.
Trial with outer superellipse power 3.0; rejected in favor of the power-3.5 geometry.
Trial with shifted inner rails, taller rail bars, and widened/repositioned junction paths; rejected because it was below the iteration-4 best.

final_geometry: Restored to iteration 4, the honest best after the six-call cap.
